body: Airline passenger group FlyersRights announced on October 30, 2026 that it had filed a petition in the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit against the US Department of Transportation (DOT), challenging a DOT rule that changes how airlines report the causes of flight delays and cancellations. Under the rule, ten types of disruption would move out of the Air Carrier category, which covers causes treated as within an airline's control.

The types include certain unscheduled maintenance, cybersecurity attacks, removal of an unruly passenger, medical emergencies not attributable to the airline, and unexpected failures of government systems. The maintenance provision covers problems outside scheduled maintenance that cannot be deferred or must be fixed before flight, including work required by an airworthiness directive, while cyberattacks qualify only if the airline complies with applicable cybersecurity regulations. FlyersRights argues that airline commitments to provide meals, hotel rooms and transportation often turn on whether a disruption was within the carrier's control, so the reclassification could shift those costs to passengers. It also argues that Congress directed a change in delay-cause reporting only, not a reduction in assistance for stranded passengers, and that DOT improperly skipped the usual public notice-and-comment process.

DOT said the exclusions were required by the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, and acknowledged in the rule that it expects airlines to provide fewer amenities and less compensation once the ten causes are excluded. The rule was published on September 3, 2026, but its effective date was postponed to February 1, 2027 after a request from Airlines for America, with the revised reporting requirements applying to flights beginning January 1, 2027; the changes had not yet taken effect at publication. FlyersRights and three other consumer organizations had previously asked DOT to withdraw the rule. Ticket refunds are separate from the meals, lodging and other assistance at issue: under DOT rules described in the article, passengers are entitled to a refund for a canceled flight, regardless of cause, if they decline alternative travel, vouchers or other compensation, and refund rights also apply to qualifying significant delays and schedule changes when passengers choose not to travel.
en.summary: FlyersRights has petitioned the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit against a DOT rule that would move ten disruption types out of the airline-controlled reporting category, arguing it would shift delay costs to passengers. The rule's effective date was postponed to February 1, 2027.
en.title: Passenger rights group sues DOT over rule shifting flight delay costs to travelers

body: 乘客團體FlyersRights於2026年10月30日宣布，已向美國哥倫比亞特區聯邦上訴法院提出請願，挑戰美國運輸部（DOT）一項改變航空公司通報航班延誤與取消原因方式的規則。根據該規則，10類干擾將移出「航空承運人」類別，該類別涵蓋被視為航空公司可控範圍內的原因。

這10類包括特定非定期維修、網路攻擊、移除鬧事乘客、非航空公司責任的醫療緊急事件，以及政府系統非預期故障。維修條款涵蓋定期維修以外的問題，且須為無法延後或起飛前必須處理者，包括適航指令要求的工作；網路攻擊則僅在航空公司符合相關網路安全法規時才適用。FlyersRights主張，航空公司提供餐食、住宿與交通的承諾，往往取決於干擾是否屬於航空公司可控範圍，因此重新分類可能把相關費用轉嫁給旅客；該團體也主張，國會僅指示改變延誤原因通報方式，並未要求減少對滯留旅客的協助，且美國運輸部不當跳過了通常的公開徵求意見程序。

美國運輸部表示，相關排除是2024年FAA重新授權法案所要求，並在規則中承認，一旦10類原因被排除，預期航空公司提供的禮遇與補償將會減少。該規則於2026年9月3日發布，但在Airlines for America提出要求後，生效日期延後至2027年2月1日，修正後的通報要求適用於2027年1月1日起的航班，發布時相關改變尚未生效。FlyersRights與另外3個消費者團體先前已要求美國運輸部撤回該規則。機票退款與上述餐食、住宿等協助是分開的：根據報導所述的美國運輸部規則，航班取消時不論原因，只要旅客拒絕替代行程、代金券或其他補償，即有權獲得退款；符合條件的重大延誤與班表變更，若旅客選擇不搭乘，也適用退款權利。
zh.summary: FlyersRights已向美國哥倫比亞特區聯邦上訴法院提出請願，挑戰美國運輸部一項將10類干擾移出航空公司可控通報類別的規則，主張此舉會把延誤費用轉嫁給旅客。該規則生效日期已延後至2027年2月1日。
